guide.title: How to record an entry
guide.intro: Choose what happened in plain words. The system files it correctly behind the scenes — you don't need accounting knowledge.
points: If you paid something now, use a "Money out" option and pick the account it left.
If you owe it but haven't paid, use "Record now, pay later" — it becomes a payable with a due date.
If a customer owes you, use "Customer receivable".
Amounts in USD save the exchange rate at that moment, so old entries never change.
Sales, COGS and profit come from Orders automatically — use "Sales income" only for sales not entered as orders.

ledger.title: Ledger guide
ledger.intro: The ledger is the full history of finance movements. It is the source for balances, reports and audit review.
points: Paid entries affect cash or bank accounts immediately.
Due entries become payables or receivables until they are settled.
Important entries should be reversed with a reason instead of deleted.

dues.title: Payables and receivables guide
dues.intro: Payables are amounts Laheeb owes others. Receivables are amounts others owe Laheeb.
points: Use Settle when a supplier is paid or a customer pays against an outstanding due.
Aging buckets help prioritize collection and supplier payment timing.
Overdue rows should be reviewed before cash planning.

accounts.title: Accounts guide
accounts.intro: Accounts are where money is stored or processed: cash boxes, bank accounts, wallets and gateways.
points: Pick the correct currency so account balances match the real account.
Opening balances should be set once when the account is created.
Archived accounts stay in history but stop appearing in new entries.

parties.title: Parties guide
parties.intro: Parties are suppliers, customers, shareholders, branches or other people/companies connected to finance movements.
points: Party links make statements, payables and receivables meaningful.
Opening balances capture money owed before the system start date.
Shareholder ownership percentage is used for capital tracking.

pnl.title: P&L guide
pnl.intro: P&L explains whether the business made money in the selected period.
points: Revenue is sales before cost; COGS is product cost tied to sold items.
Gross profit is revenue minus COGS.
Operating profit subtracts operating expenses from gross profit.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet guide
balanceSheet.intro: The balance sheet shows what Laheeb owns, owes and keeps as equity.
points: Assets include cash, bank, receivables and inventory value.
Liabilities are payables still owed to suppliers or others.
Equity includes capital plus retained earnings.

audit.title: Audit and reversal guide
audit.intro: Finance history is preserved for control. Corrections should be explained and visible.
points: Creates, edits, settlements, exports and reversals are logged with user and time.
Reversal keeps the original entry and adds a reversal marker instead of deleting it.
Use the reason field to explain why the correction was needed.

hub.title: Data management guide
hub.intro: Start here when you need to create, clean up or review operating records. Each section opens the focused workflow for that record type.
points: Use Products & Variations before selling a new item.
Use Orders for sales, invoices, customer history, stock deduction and finance sync.
Use Inventory and Roast batches to keep stock, cost layers and production accurate.
Use Branches & Franchises and System lists for controlled setup data.

products.title: How to use Products & Variations
products.intro: A main product is the umbrella (e.g. Turkish Coffee). A variation is what you actually sell (e.g. 250g · Cardamom · Medium). Start with the main product, then add its variations.
points: Create the main product first, then open it to add variations.
Each variation carries its own selling price, cost recipe and inventory link.
Only active, configured variations appear when creating an order.
Editing a variation's cost only affects future orders — past orders keep their snapshot.
Variations don't need a main product; standalone ones show under "Ungrouped variations".

orders.title: How to use Orders
orders.intro: Record every order with its line items. Totals, invoices, stock and reports all update from what you enter here.
points: Pick the customer, then add variations as line items with quantity and price.
Completed orders deduct stock automatically; pending/cancelled orders don't.
Editing or cancelling an order re-computes its totals and reverses its stock.
The order number is permanent once created.

customers.title: How to use Customers
customers.intro: Customers link orders to people and businesses, powering CRM and repeat-purchase insights.
points: Each customer gets a permanent ID (CL-000001) used across orders and reports.
Enter the phone and address so invoices and delivery are accurate.
Set the source to track which campaign or channel brought them in.
Search by name or phone before adding, to avoid duplicates.

inventory.title: How to use Inventory
inventory.intro: Inventory items are green beans, roasted beans, packaging and finished goods. Stock is the running sum of all movements.
points: Use "Receive stock" to add quantity at a cost — this creates a FIFO cost layer.
Sales and production deduct stock; the active cost follows the oldest layer.
Set a reorder point to get low-stock alerts on the dashboard.
Link a finished-goods item to a variation so sales deduct it automatically.

batches.title: How to use Roast Batches
batches.intro: Log each roast: green beans in, roasted beans out. Roast loss and the roasted-bean cost are derived from this.
points: Enter green input and roasted output to compute yield and shrinkage.
Higher roast loss raises the cost per kg of roasted beans.
Link the batch to the variations it produces for accurate costing.

systemLists.title: About System lists
systemLists.intro: These are the standard categories used across the app (channels, governorates, grinds, roast levels, categories).
points: They keep reports and filters consistent everywhere.
Owners and Admins can rename values (EN + AR), reorder, hide, add and merge them.
Built-in values and values used in old records can't be deleted — archive or merge them instead.
Every change is recorded in the audit log.

guide.title: How to use Branches & Franchises
guide.intro: Branches are your HQ, company-owned shops and franchise locations. Their code links orders, users and reports, so set it carefully.
points: Pick the type: Headquarters, Company-owned, or Franchise.
The branch code is permanent once set — it ties orders, users and reports together.
Franchise contact and agreement fields appear only for franchise branches.
Franchise accounts see only their own branch's data; HQ sees all branches.
A branch with orders, users or stock can't be deleted — deactivate it instead; history stays linked.

health.title: Imported finance health
health.unassigned: Not tied to a cash account
health.confirm: Remove duplicate imported rows? The earliest of each identical set is kept. This cannot be undone.
health.verdictClean: No duplicate imported rows. The "Unassigned (imported)" total is simply imported purchases that aren't tied to a cash account, minus account-less capital — not duplication. Assign those purchases to a cash account from Finance → Ledger, or record the funding capital, to resolve it.
health.verdictDupes: Found exact-duplicate imported rows — usually from mixing manual entry with imports. Removing them keeps the earliest of each identical set.

reset.title: Danger zone — reset all data
reset.body: Permanently deletes products, product groups, customers, orders, inventory + stock, batches, finance entries, cash accounts, suppliers/shareholders, offers, shipments, and upload/sync history. Keeps your users, branches, settings and connectors. This cannot be undone — type RESET to confirm.
reset.done: All business data has been cleared.
reset.forbidden: Only the Owner can reset data.

invoice.title: Invoice
invoice.guideText: Each item shows its quantity, selling unit, unit price and total. The payment section shows how much was paid and what the customer still owes. Record every later payment so Finance and customer statements stay updated.
